subject: Civil Engineering
title: Shotcrete: Sprayed Concrete Lining
description: A 60-second lesson on Shotcrete: Sprayed Concrete Lining.

hook.text: Seconds after blasting, wet concrete is sprayed onto raw rock — instant support.

buildup.text: Shotcrete is concrete projected at high velocity from a nozzle — it sticks to any surface.

discovery.text: Steel fibers mixed in replace traditional rebar — tougher, faster, and no formwork needed.

twist.text: Accelerators make shotcrete set in minutes — critical when loose rock could fall at any moment.

climax.text: Layer by layer, shotcrete builds up to a structural lining — 300mm thick or more.

punchline.text: Spray concrete on rock and it becomes a wall in minutes. Speed is survival underground.

quiz.question: Why is shotcrete preferred for immediate tunnel support after excavation?
options: It's cheaper than all other lining methods
It can be sprayed rapidly onto any surface without formwork, setting in minutes
Shotcrete is stronger than precast concrete segments

details.summary: Shotcrete is concrete pneumatically sprayed at high velocity onto tunnel walls immediately after excavation to provide rapid structural support. It conforms to irregular rock surfaces, bonds to the ground, and gains strength within hours.
details.whyItMatters: Shotcrete's ability to provide immediate structural support to freshly excavated ground revolutionized tunnel construction speed and safety. It is now used in virtually every modern tunnel project.
takeaways: Shotcrete gains useful strength within 1-4 hours of application
Steel fiber reinforcement replaces traditional mesh for faster application
Typical shotcrete thickness ranges from 50-300 mm depending on ground conditions

faq.question: How is shotcrete different from regular poured concrete?
faq.answer: Shotcrete is the same material as conventional concrete but applied by spraying at high velocity through a nozzle. The impact compacts the concrete against the surface without formwork. Accelerating admixtures speed initial set. The application method allows immediate placement on any surface shape.

faq.question: What is the difference between wet-mix and dry-mix shotcrete?
faq.answer: In wet-mix, all ingredients including water are mixed before pumping to the nozzle where compressed air propels it. In dry-mix, dry ingredients are fed to the nozzle where water is added at the point of discharge. Wet-mix produces less dust and waste, dominating modern tunnel applications.
